title: +PSYCHOLOGY OF TRAUMA, OPPRESSION, AND RESILIENCE
description: Focuses on the psychological science of humans' reactions to traumatic events. Critically examines the social and cultural context for those events and reactions, including systemic racism, sexism, and other forms of oppression. Explores the psychological science of healing, resilience, and liberation, in the context of evidence-based clinical psychological treatments, institutional courage, and societal change.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: (PSY 201, 201H, 201Z or 201HZ) and (PSY 202, 202H, 202Z or 202HZ).
A minimum grade of C- is required in PSY 201, PSY 201H, PSY 201Z, PSY 201HZ, PSY 202, PSY 202H, PSY 202Z and PSY 202HZ.

Students with a term class standing of Freshman or Sophomore may not enroll.
recommendations: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course
attribute_description: Core Education - Difference, Power, & Oppression: Advanced (CSDP)
